title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40934v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In this work, we provide a formal framework and mathematical definition for the subset of foundation models focused on enabling the property of "any-task inference" (ATI) (similar to zero-shot inference), rather than those designed for pre-training fine-tuning. To achieve this mathematical definition, we formalize the notion of a "space of tasks of interest," which we include in the problem domain, then provide an interface-based formal definition for ATI foundation models as those that map samples of data $x$ and tasks $t$ to predictions over the space of labels directly. While simple, this definition allows us to show that all ATI foundation models can be decomposed through a "universal task reduction" lens into encoder, model, and decoder aspects. translated_title: 理解与构建具备“任意任务推理”能力的基础模型的理论框架
translated_abstract: 在本工作中，我们为一类专注于实现“任意任务推理”（ATI）（类似于零样本推理）属性的基础模型子集提供了一个形式化框架和数学定义，而非针对那些为预训练-微调流程设计的模型。为实现这一数学定义，我们形式化了“感兴趣任务空间”的概念并将其纳入问题域中，然后给出了ATI基础模型的基于接口的形式化定义，即那些将数据样本 $x$ 和任务 $t$ 直接映射到标签空间上的预测的模型。虽然这一定义简单，但它使我们能够证明所有ATI基础模型都可以通过“通用任务约简”的视角分解为编码器、模型和解码器三个部分。我们可以利用这一分解，将基础模型的误差也分解为与该约简不同方面相对应的各项，并将其分层为一系列“设计项”，
tldr: 本文为具备“任意任务推理”（ATI）能力的基础模型提供了形式化的数学定义框架，证明所有此类模型均可通过“通用任务约简”分解为编码器、模型和解码器三个部分，并据此将模型误差分解为不同的设计项。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a formal mathematical framework for "any-task inference" (ATI) capable foundation models, showing that all such models can be decomposed through a "universal task reduction" lens into encoder, model, and decoder aspects, enabling foundation model error to be stratified into distinct design terms.
